Jim Cramer warned that Nvidia *($NVDA)*'s blockbuster earnings may not be enough to win back investors, arguing that Jensen Huang's departure and Anthropic's upcoming IPO are creating new headwinds for the stock.

• *Earnings Aren't Enough:* “The numbers weren't good; they were fabulous. But it doesn't matter,” Cramer said, arguing that investors have effectively voted Nvidia out of their portfolios.
• *Anthropic Competition:* With Anthropic *($ANT)* set to begin trading Thursday, Cramer believes investors have an attractive new way to gain AI exposure, potentially drawing capital away from Nvidia.
• *Leadership Uncertainty:* Despite praising interim CEO Colette Kress, Cramer said investors want permanent leadership and remain concerned about Nvidia's future without Huang.
• *Investor Sentiment:* “People want a company with a permanent CEO, and they want Jensen Huang,” Cramer said. Rather than wait for the board's CEO search, he believes investors “would rather just get some Anthropic.”

TRUMP: SPOKE TO XI ABOUT CHIPS, AI LAST NIGHT

TRUMP: DIDN'T DISCUSS HUANG WITH XI'

TRUMP ON JENSEN HUANG: SOME PEOPLE CAN'T BE REPLACED
TRUMP: COULD SELL BLACKWELLS IN 2, 3 YEARS

TRUMP: INDICATION THAT IRAN WAS LOOKING AT GASES, BIO WEAPONS

TRUMP ON BIOWEAPONS: PEOPLE SHOULDN'T BE PANICKED ABOUT THIS KIND OF THING

Trump called Jensen Huang's removal from Nvidia *($NVDA)* a “tragedy,” describing him as irreplaceable and urging greater protection for America's leading innovators during a Fox News interview from Shenzhen, China.

• *Talks With Xi:* Trump said he did not discuss Huang's situation with Chinese President Xi Jinping, though he may have briefly mentioned it. “It's such a tragedy. He's such a brilliant man.”
• *Nvidia's Board:* Trump acknowledged directors have their own views but argued, “Some people can't be replaced,” describing Huang as a decade ahead of competitors.
• *Blackwell Technology:* Trump claimed Nvidia's Blackwell chip is 10 years ahead of rivals and too technologically complex to copy, contrasting it with widespread product piracy.
• *Protecting Innovators:* “We have to take care of our geniuses,” Trump said, arguing that exceptional talent deserves support despite personal controversies.
• *Elon Musk Comparison:* Trump claimed he helped Musk overcome major difficulties during his first term, crediting that support with helping enable SpaceX's advances in reusable rockets.

Trump said he has not heard allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and defended allowing Nvidia *($NVDA)* to sell chips to China, suggesting Blackwell exports could be permitted in two to three years.

• *Alice Huang:* “I haven't heard that she was a spy. She was a businesswoman who bought chips,” Trump said, adding that he did not know whether those purchases were legitimate.
• *China Chip Sales:* “We allow them to buy. In fact, encourage. We want to make money,” Trump said, arguing Nvidia should be allowed to sell chips while restricting its most advanced technology.
• *Blackwell Timeline:* Trump suggested he could permit Blackwell sales to China in two or three years if he remained in office, but announced no immediate policy change.

*Trump said there are indications Iran is exploring chemical and biological weapons as the U.S. restricts its nuclear capabilities, responding to questions about a reported Iranian dirty-bomb plot targeting Washington.*

• *Iranian Weapons:* “There is indication that Iran is looking at gases, looking at bio,” Trump said, suggesting Tehran is pursuing alternatives after nuclear restrictions.
• *D.C. Threat:* Asked whether Washington residents should panic, Trump reportedly responded, “I don't think so, no,” adding: “If it does happen, we wipe them out.”
• *Potential Escalation:* Trump said, “We'll see what happens after January 1st,” without specifying a deadline or announcing military action.

Nvidia *($NVDA)* announced two new multibillion-dollar supply-chain commitments in Taiwan, securing additional advanced chip substrates and packaging capacity for future AI platforms.

• *Kinsus (TWSE: 3189) — Over $1B:* Nvidia is providing more than $1B to expand advanced substrate production at Kinsus' Taoyuan facility. Nvidia-dedicated capacity will increase more than 3.5x, with production starting in H2 2027 and further expansion targeted for Q3 2028.
• *SPIL (NYSE: $ASX) — Multibillion-Dollar Deal:* Nvidia signed a new multiyear agreement with Siliconware Precision, a subsidiary of U.S.-listed ASE Technology Holding *($ASX)*, to triple advanced packaging capacity in Taiwan by mid-2029. Funding covers production lines, interposer fabrication, assembly and testing.
• *Long-Term Supply:* Kinsus said the investment aims to secure substrate availability through at least 2030, with additional expansion investments under discussion.
• *What's New:* Both agreements were first disclosed November 17, with additional details November 18. SPIL's packaging expansion is separate from its previously announced optical-engine capacity expansion.

*U.S. equity futures rebounded Wednesday night ahead of Anthropic's historic IPO, led by technology stocks, while Asian markets traded unevenly and cryptocurrencies remained under pressure. Fresh cybersecurity earnings also sparked significant after-hours moves.*

• *U.S. Futures:* Nasdaq-100 rose 0.63% (+170.6) to 27,286.9, S&P 500 gained 0.38% (+27.6) to 7,351.1, and Dow futures advanced 0.34% (+172) to 50,445.
• *Asian Markets:* South Korea's KOSPI fell 1.99% and KOSDAQ lost 1.85%, while Japan's Nikkei slipped 0.41% in the latest supplied snapshot. South Korea opened an hour late for its national college entrance exam.
• *Crypto & Metals:* Bitcoin traded near $62,472 (-2.84%) and Ethereum near $1,768 (-1.94%). Gold rebounded 0.44% to $3,741/oz, while silver gained 0.34% to $45.21.

• *Cybersecurity Rally:* Palo Alto Networks *($PANW)* jumped roughly 9% after hours after reporting $3.44B in quarterly revenue, raising FY2027 guidance to $14.52B–$14.57B and announcing a $4.5B acquisition of AI startup Applied Compute. CrowdStrike *($CRWD)* gained about 5%, Zscaler *($ZS)* 3% and Fortinet *($FTNT)* 2%.
• *Other After-Hours Movers:* Everpure *($P)* gained approximately 3%–4% after beating earnings expectations and raising guidance. Magnera *($MAGN)* rose about 14% following results showing stronger adjusted EBITDA and cash flow. Red Robin *($RRGB)* plunged roughly 17.5% after missing revenue and earnings estimates.

• *Anthropic IPO:* Anthropic *($ANT)* priced its offering at $83 per share, raising approximately $81.3B in the largest IPO on record. Trading begins Thursday, November 19. Cboe expects options trading could begin Monday, November 23, pending readiness.
• *Thursday Catalysts:* Investors await Anthropic's first trading session, weekly jobless claims and earnings from Walmart *($WMT)*, Alibaba *($BABA)* and PDD *($PDD)* before the U.S. open, followed by Gap *($GAP)* and Ross Stores *($ROST)* after the close.

Trump said the U.S. could allow Nvidia *($NVDA)* to sell Blackwell AI chips to China in 2–3 years, once newer processors surpass them. No immediate policy change was announced, Bloomberg reports.

• *Blackwell Timeline:* “In two years or three years, I would, if I were here, I would say, go ahead. You can now sell Blackwells because they'll have something else,” Trump said.
• *Technology Shift:* Trump said Nvidia is already developing Blackwell's successor and suggested the current generation could become obsolete within a year.
• *China Restrictions:* Washington previously permitted older H200 exports but blocked Blackwell sales. “They didn't even sell that many, the 200s, and the 200s are old now,” Trump said.
• *Tighter Controls:* The administration recently expanded restrictions targeting Chinese access to advanced AI chips through overseas data centers.
• *Congressional Action:* Republican Sen. Jim Banks and Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren are advancing the AI Overwatch Act, which would restrict Blackwell exports to China for at least 18 months. The proposal is under negotiation for inclusion in December's defense package.

*Wall Street's $500B Nvidia *($NVDA)* chip-financing initiative has yet to deploy any capital, with its first deal unlikely to close before 2027. The program was designed to help AI customers finance chip purchases, sustain Nvidia's growth and support its valuation, The Wall Street Journal reports.*

• *$500B Agreement:* Apollo *($APO)*, Blackstone *($BX)*, BlackRock *($BLK)*, Brookfield *($BN)*, Goldman Sachs *($GS)* and KKR *($KKR)* signed an August memorandum outlining a fundraising target, not binding capital commitments.
• *Financing Roadblock:* Nvidia offered credit support covering up to 25% of project costs, but lenders increasingly want stronger guarantees. Broadcom *($AVGO)* provided an approximately 85% residual-value guarantee for Anthropic's $35B chip-financing deal and nearly 75% for a separate $63B deal.
• *Huang's Strategy:* Former CEO Jensen Huang pushed the initiative amid concerns over Nvidia's declining valuation multiple. An earlier proposed $250B backstop for an OpenAI data center triggered a 5% stock selloff, prompting Nvidia to halve its initial financial commitment, WSJ reports.
• *Leadership Shift:* Interim CEO Colette Kress is taking a more cautious approach. “We are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees,” she told investors.
• *Neocloud Risk:* Apollo CEO Marc Rowan warned that without Nvidia's financing guarantees, access to capital for many neocloud providers could disappear. Negotiations for the first chip-backed deal remain ongoing, with no closing expected before 2027.
• *Market Implications:* Nvidia's earnings and outlook remain strong, but tighter financing conditions could constrain customers' ability to fund future GPU purchases, even if the broader $500B initiative never fully materializes.

*Trump is weighing renewed joint U.S.-Israeli strikes against Iran as Israel warns of expanding chemical weapons research, while Gulf nations urge restraint over fears of retaliation against regional energy infrastructure, Axios reports.*

• *Military Options:* Trump requested assessments of Iran's likely retaliation, particularly against Gulf oil and gas facilities.
• *Israeli Pressure:* Netanyahu is pushing for swift military action. Mossad chief Roman Gofman met U.S. officials and presented intelligence alleging increased Iranian chemical weapons research and testing.
• *Intelligence Disputes:* U.S. and Israeli officials acknowledge increased Iranian chemical weapons activity but say Tehran currently lacks the capability to launch such attacks. Some U.S. officials questioned Israel's intelligence and its urgency.
• *U.S. Divisions:* Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth favors stronger military action, while Gulf leaders advocate continued economic pressure. Trump said Wednesday, “We'll see what happens after January 1.”
• *Regional Escalation:* Iran has resumed drone attacks on U.S. bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Maritime tensions in the Strait of Hormuz are also rising.
• *Diplomatic Efforts:* Qatari and Pakistani mediators continue seeking a U.S.-Iran agreement, but recent talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi produced no significant progress. CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper also met Israeli and Saudi officials to coordinate regional security.

*Trump defended AI development at the APEC summit, warning against regulations that could stifle innovation while acknowledging potential risks. He also highlighted falling inflation, U.S. economic priorities in the Pacific and anticipated meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.*

• *AI Regulation:* Trump described AI as overwhelmingly positive but said its potential downsides require careful management. He opposed regulations that would “stifle” AI development, declaring his administration would not allow that to happen.
• *Inflation:* Trump said inflation had fallen more than anticipated over the past three months, without providing specific figures.
• *U.S. Pacific Strategy:* Trump reaffirmed America's commitment to strengthening economic growth, sovereignty, stability, prosperity and peaceful development throughout the region.
• *Global Diplomacy:* Trump said he looks forward to meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

*Wealthy family offices increased their stock allocations to 36.4% in Q3 2026, their largest portfolio holding, while reducing private-market exposure and limiting AI-related risk, according to CNBC's Family Office Portfolio Tracker.*

• *Stock Allocations:* Public equities rose to 36.4% from 35.6% in Q2 and 33.6% in 2024. Public markets now represent 53.1% of portfolios versus 46.8% in alternatives.
• *AI Risk Management:* Technology accounts for 28% of family-office stock portfolios versus 40% of the S&P 500. Financials represent 18%, compared with 11% in the index, providing a potential offset to AI-related volatility.
• *Private Markets Decline:* Alternative allocations fell from 48.5% a year ago to 46.8%. Real estate dropped to 7.2% from 9.4%, hedge funds to 7.5% and private equity to 6.4%. Direct private-company holdings remain the largest alternative allocation at 15.7%.
• *Cash & Bonds:* Cash increased to 8.6%, providing liquidity for potential opportunities, while fixed income rose for a third consecutive quarter to 8.1%.
• *Investor Positioning:* Addepar CEO Eric Poirier said family offices remain invested despite AI bubble concerns: “They're fading the AI trade to some extent, but still staying quite exposed.”
• *Data Scope:* The tracker covers hundreds of family offices managing more than $1.4T in assets. Allocation changes reflect both market performance and investment decisions, not necessarily new stock purchases.

Nasdaq-100 futures surged 2% Thursday as Anthropic's record $81.3B IPO pricing revived enthusiasm for AI stocks. Semiconductors, neoclouds and cybersecurity shares rallied ahead of Anthropic *($ANT)*'s Nasdaq debut.

• *U.S. Futures — 6:38 AM CT:* Nasdaq-100 +2.00% to 27,659.8; S&P 500 +1.15% to 7,408.1; Dow +0.60% (+302) to 50,575. VIX fell 9.04% to 22.34.
• *Anthropic IPO:* The Claude developer priced 980M shares at $83, above its $70–$78 range, raising $81.3B and implying a valuation near $1.5T. Early investor enthusiasm lifted Alphabet *($GOOGL)* 3.9% and Amazon *($AMZN)* 2.2%, both Anthropic investors.
• *AI Chip Rebound:* Nvidia *($NVDA)* gained roughly 1.8%, while Intel *($INTC)*, AMD *($AMD)*, Micron *($MU)* and Marvell *($MRVL)* rose approximately 3%–5%, recovering alongside broader AI sentiment.
• *Neoclouds & Data Centers:* CoreWeave *($CRWV)* and Nebius *($NBIS)* gained 4.8%, while IREN *($IREN)* and Applied Digital *($APLD)* rose 5.4%. Texas also resumed normal data-center permit reviews, easing concerns about delayed AI infrastructure projects.
• *Cybersecurity:* Palo Alto Networks *($PANW)* surged roughly 10% after raising FY2027 revenue guidance and announcing a $4.5B acquisition of Applied Compute. CrowdStrike *($CRWD)*, Cloudflare *($NET)*, Okta *($OKTA)* and Zscaler *($ZS)* climbed approximately 4.5%–7%.
• *Earnings Movers:* NetEase *($NTES)* fell roughly 5% after missing earnings estimates. Alibaba *($BABA)* traded lower despite 53% AI cloud revenue growth, as adjusted earnings missed expectations. SELLAS Life Sciences *($SLS)* dropped after pricing a $150M equity offering.

Three Wall Street firms initiated bullish coverage of Anthropic *($ANT)* ahead of its Nasdaq debut Thursday, projecting 51%–87% upside from its $83 IPO price. The AI developer raised $81.3B in its record-sized offering, CNBC reports.

• *Analyst Targets:* Wolfe Research initiated Outperform with a $135 target (+63%); Citizens assigned Market Outperform at $125 (+51%); Melius Research rated Buy with a $155 target (+87%).
• *Wolfe's Outlook:* Analyst Alex Zukin called Anthropic a potentially “category defining company,” citing its massive addressable market, rapid growth and potential to generate exceptional new revenue by 2028.
• *Melius' Thesis:* Ben Reitzes sees Anthropic as exceptionally positioned to monetize AI as enterprises integrate Claude into core business operations.
• *Citizens' Forecast:* Patrick Walravens highlighted management stability, with all seven co-founders still involved. Citizens projects revenue of $52.5B in 2026 (+1,000% YoY), $137B in 2027 and $417.8B by 2029.
• *IPO Details:* Anthropic priced 980M shares at $83, above its expected $70–$78 range. The $81.3B gross offering exceeds SpaceX's previous IPO record.

Walmart *($WMT)* reported additional Q3 FY2027 strength in operating profit, international sales and advertising, while higher inventory and weaker free cash flow highlighted costs heading into the holiday season.

• *Operating Profit:* Adjusted operating income reached $7.77B, beating estimates of $7.54B. Gross profit margin improved 28 basis points.
• *International Growth:* Revenue rose 7% to $35.9B, despite Flipkart's Big Billion Days timing reducing quarterly growth by approximately 500 basis points. A corresponding benefit is expected in Q4.
• *Sam's Club & Advertising:* Sam's Club comparable sales excluding fuel increased 4.9%, while global advertising revenue grew 25%.
• *Cash Flow:* Nine-month operating cash flow rose $2B to $29.4B, while free cash flow declined $2B to $6.8B.
• *Inventory:* Global inventory increased 8.1%, reflecting holiday event timing, strategic initiatives and cost inflation.
• *Holiday Outlook:* Walmart's main Black Friday event begins online Monday, November 23, with Walmart+ members receiving early access to select deals.

Walmart *($WMT)* raised its full-year sales and earnings outlook after beating Q3 expectations, citing market-share gains, strong e-commerce growth and improving digital profitability ahead of the holidays, CNBC reports.

• *Q3 Earnings:* Revenue rose 5.2% to $188.84B, beating estimates of $187.27B. Adjusted EPS reached $0.65 versus $0.64 expected, while net income fell to $4.95B from $6.14B.
• *Raised Guidance:* Walmart now expects FY sales growth of 4.9%–5.2%, adjusted EPS of $2.84–$2.89 and adjusted operating income growth of 8%–8.6%, all above previous forecasts.
• *E-Commerce Growth:* Global online sales rose 17%, led by Walmart U.S. (+23%) and Sam's Club (+30%). U.S. advertising revenue climbed 37%, while Walmart U.S. comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.9%.
• *Consumer Spending:* Walmart rolled back prices on nearly 8,000 products and recorded its strongest food market-share gains in three years. Tariff refunds helped offset higher diesel and transportation costs.
• *AI Shopping:* CEO John Furner said customers using Walmart's Sparky AI assistant have baskets averaging 40% larger, highlighting growing adoption ahead of the holidays.
• *Sam's Club:* Revenue climbed 10% to $25.9B. Walmart's new joint membership program reportedly brought roughly 2M additional people into Sam's Club, while global membership-fee revenue rose 17%.

TSMC *($TSM)* and Samsung have suspended shipments of certain advanced chips to Chinese customers while seeking U.S. export licenses under new Commerce Department restrictions, threatening further disruptions to China's AI and consumer electronics supply chains.

• *New U.S. Rules:* The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) now requires licenses for covered advanced chips made using American technology and ultimately shipped to China, eliminating previous exemptions.
• *AI Chip Restrictions:* Chinese designers can no longer use independent packaging and testing firms to verify that chips fall outside U.S. controls and avoid direct licensing. Samsung customers include Baidu's Kunlun AI unit and ByteDance.
• *Smartphone Impact:* The removal of exemptions for non-AI applications also affects advanced consumer chips. TSMC supplies Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo, while both manufacturers have notified some consumer electronics customers of shipment suspensions.
• *Supply Pressure:* The restrictions compound China's existing memory-chip price surge and capacity constraints at domestic foundries including SMIC.
• *License Outlook:* Industry sources expect U.S. approval for consumer smartphone chips, but licensing delays could disrupt production. TSMC did not respond to requests for comment; Samsung declined to comment.

China's Moonshot AI, developer of the Kimi models, scrapped a $150M agreement to access Nvidia *($NVDA)* Blackwell Ultra B300 chips through an Indonesian data center following new U.S. restrictions on Chinese companies' access to advanced AI computing abroad, The Information reports.

• *Canceled Deal:* Moonshot had contracted with a Southeast Asian neocloud to rent a large cluster of B300 GPUs, with access expected as early as 2027.
• *U.S. Restrictions:* The Commerce Department's new rule closes a loophole allowing Chinese companies to remotely use advanced Nvidia chips at overseas data centers despite restrictions on direct exports to China.
• *AI Development Impact:* The cancellation removes a planned source of high-performance computing for Moonshot, adding pressure on Chinese AI developers already facing limited access to leading U.S. processors.

Uber Eats *($UBER)* launched its first auto parts category through a partnership with AutoParts.com, offering on-demand and scheduled delivery from nearly 7,000 participating U.S. locations.

• *Nationwide Network:* Customers can order automotive parts through Uber Eats using AutoParts.com's network of distributors, independent suppliers and retailers, with real-time delivery tracking.
• *Retail Expansion:* The partnership extends Uber Eats beyond groceries, electronics and home improvement into automotive supplies, targeting urgent repairs and routine maintenance.
• *Launch Promotion:* Uber Eats is offering 20% off AutoParts.com orders of $60 or more, capped at $20. Eligible Uber One orders retain $0 delivery fees and membership benefits.
• *Management Commentary:* Uber Eats executive Prashant Garg called auto parts a “natural extension” of its marketplace, emphasizing faster access when vehicle problems arise.

Coherent Corp. *($COHR)* authorized a new share repurchase program of up to $2B, according to an SEC filing released Thursday morning.

• *Buyback Terms:* The board approved the program November 18. Shares may be repurchased through open-market transactions, negotiated purchases or accelerated buybacks.
• *No Deadline:* The authorization has no expiration date, requires no minimum purchases and can be suspended or discontinued at any time.
• *Nvidia Connection:* The buyback is separate from Nvidia's *($NVDA)* $2B equity investment in Coherent announced in March to support advanced optical technology and AI infrastructure expansion.

*Samsung Electronics dismissed AI bubble concerns, citing sustained demand, long-term chip contracts and limited exposure to heavily indebted neocloud providers. It also expects semiconductor shortages to persist.*

• *AI Demand:* “Today's investment is not a result of speculation, but actual tangible demand,” executive Kang Suk-chae said, describing AI spending as structural rather than cyclical.
• *Neocloud Risk:* Samsung estimates neoclouds, including CoreWeave *($CRWV)*, represent just 8% of the market. “We do not expect these concerns to pose a significant threat to the broader AI growth trajectory.”
• *Chip Supply:* Samsung expects shortages to “persist for the foreseeable future,” highlighting its memory, advanced packaging and diversified foundry capabilities in competing with TSMC *($TSM)*.
• *Shareholder Returns:* Samsung plans a “substantial” share buyback and cancellation program alongside dividends, with details expected in January after reviewing capital spending needs.

STMicroelectronics *($STM)* outlined a broader recovery driven by automotive electrification, industrial automation and satellite communications, alongside a major European manufacturing overhaul targeting higher profitability.

• *Growth Outlook:* Industrial revenue is expected to add roughly $1B in 2027, while automotive sales are projected to grow by high single digits, supported by electric vehicles and higher chip content.
• *Satellite Demand:* Low Earth orbit communications revenue exceeded $1B in 2026. Demand remains strong, but manufacturing constraints could limit 2027 growth.
• *Factory Restructuring:* STM plans to close four older 8-inch fabs while expanding 300mm production at Crolles and Agrate, targeting approximately 400 basis points of margin improvement.
• *Financial Targets:* Q4 revenue is projected at $4.15B (+25% YoY), with gross margin near 39%. Management targets 44%–46% margins at an $18B annual revenue run rate as restructuring benefits emerge in 2028.
• *Consumer Weakness:* Personal electronics remains pressured, with global smartphone shipments expected to decline 6%–7% in 2027. A potential recovery could begin in 2028.

STMicroelectronics *($STM)* expects data-center revenue to more than double in 2027, with CEO Jean-Marc Chery reporting no change in customer demand or commitments following the U.S. midterm elections.

• *Demand Unchanged:* Chery reported “absolutely no” change in order backlogs or long-term agreements and “zero impact” on customer behavior despite concerns about tighter U.S. data-center regulations.
• *Revenue Outlook:* Data-center sales are projected to rise from $1.3B in 2026 to $2.8B in 2027, potentially reaching $3B if supply constraints ease.
• *Growth Drivers:* Silicon photonics leads demand, followed by microcontrollers, ASICs and power components. STM serves more than 10 data-center customers, with none contributing over 30% of annual segment revenue.
• *AI Financing:* Chery defended infrastructure spending, arguing that hyperscalers and neoclouds primarily finance expansion through cash flow and conventional debt rather than circular financing.

Lynx Equity analyst KC Rajkumar named Micron *($MU)* his top semiconductor pick, maintaining a $1,325 price target and calling its valuation “ridiculously cheap” amid an AI-related chip selloff. 

• *Micron Valuation:* Shares trade at roughly 2.3x Rajkumar's estimated 2028 earnings. He sees the pullback as a buying opportunity, with long-term DRAM and NAND demand intact.
• *Data Center Concerns:* Rajkumar argues slower permitting has hurt chip valuations without materially changing multi-year demand forecasts.
• *Other Chip Picks:* He maintained targets of $2,450 for SanDisk *($SNDK)* and $400 for Lam Research *($LRCX)*.
• *CPU Demand:* Rajkumar is increasingly positive on AMD *($AMD)* and Intel *($INTC)*, expecting high-core-count server demand to remain resilient even if Nvidia GPU spending slows.

Lynx Equity analyst KC Rajkumar believes Anthropic's *($ANT)* IPO could revive enthusiasm for AI stocks and strengthen funding for infrastructure expansion, despite recent concerns over data-center construction delays.

• *IPO Catalyst:* Rajkumar argues a strong debut could restore investor confidence, while a higher valuation could improve Anthropic's ability to raise capital for existing infrastructure commitments.
• *Industry Backing:* Seven technology companies are reportedly investing $26B through a private placement tied to IPO pricing. Rajkumar expects industry support to continue after the debut.
• *Demand Outlook:* Rajkumar sees little evidence that slower data-center permitting has weakened long-term AI infrastructure demand.
• *Next Catalysts:* Upcoming semiconductor investor conferences could reinforce existing industry forecasts and help restore confidence.

(PSA) Retail investors receiving Anthropic *($ANT)* IPO shares at the $83 offering price could face brokerage penalties for selling too quickly, including restrictions or permanent bans from future IPO allocations, CNBC reports.

• *Fidelity:* Selling within 15 calendar days triggers a 6-month IPO ban for the first violation, 1 year for the second and a permanent ban for the third. Selling from day 16 avoids the restriction.
• *Robinhood *($HOOD)*:* Selling allocated IPO shares within 30 days may trigger a 60-day restriction on future IPO participation.
• *SoFi *($SOFI)*:* Selling within 30 days may result in a 6-month ban, then 12 months, followed by a possible permanent restriction.
• *E*TRADE:* Prefers a 30-day holding period. Early sales may affect future IPO eligibility, but no fixed penalty is specified.
• *Charles Schwab *($SCHW)*:* Confirmed no anti-flipping restriction applies to Anthropic's IPO.
• *Important Distinction:* These policies apply to shares allocated at the IPO price, not shares purchased after public trading begins.

Anthropic's *($ANT)* record IPO pushed the combined estimated wealth of its seven co-founders above $140B, approximately $20B each, based on the $83 offering price, Bloomberg reports.

• *Founder Ownership:* Each holds approximately 1.3% of Anthropic on a fully diluted basis, making all seven members of Bloomberg's 500 richest people.
• *Voting Control:* Despite their relatively small economic stakes, the founders control 50.1% of voting power through a special Class F share, provided they retain the required ownership threshold.
• *IPO Cash-Out:* Each founder sold approximately $280M in shares during the offering. Additional holdings remain subject to lockups of up to one year for founders and six months for employees.
• *Philanthropy:* All seven pledged 80% of their personal company equity to charitable causes, although the commitments are voluntary, revocable and not legally binding.

*Walmart *($WMT)* reported increased purchases of propane, bottled water and camping gear earlier this month as technology outages and viral emergency-preparedness warnings fueled stockpiling, Bloomberg reports.*

• *Demand Cooling:* CFO John David Rainey said preparedness buying has already eased and largely represents purchases brought forward from future demand.
• *Financial Impact:* The temporary sales boost did not change Walmart's current-quarter outlook, despite similar stockpiling trends reported by Costco *($COST)*.

*Trump told Chinese President Xi Jinping that the U.S. “does not support Taiwan independence” during talks in Shenzhen, according to China's state-run Xinhua News Agency.*

• *Xi's Warning:* Xi urged Washington to handle Taiwan carefully to avoid major setbacks in U.S.-China relations.
• *Chinese Commentary:* Former Global Times editor Hu Xijin argued that Taiwan's strategic value to Washington is declining as U.S.-China relations become a greater priority.
• *Key Distinction:* Trump reportedly said it “does not support” Taiwan independence, while Beijing has sought the stronger wording “opposes” independence. No U.S. confirmation or new Taiwan policy was announced.
• *Broader Talks:* China's readout also highlighted cooperation on trade, agriculture, energy, fentanyl and advanced AI.

*Chinese President Xi Jinping warned Trump that Washington must “do the right thing” on Taiwan to avoid major setbacks in U.S.-China relations, while calling for stronger cooperation on trade, AI and regional stability, according to China's Xinhua News Agency.*

• *Taiwan Warning:* Xi urged Washington to avoid disrupting bilateral ties. China's readout said Trump reiterated that the U.S. does not support Taiwan independence, consistent with longstanding U.S. policy.
• *Bilateral Action Plan:* China said both leaders agreed to develop an action plan to strengthen relations, expand cooperation and manage unresolved disputes without escalation.
• *AI Cooperation:* Xi called for coordination on AI safety and maintaining human control over the technology.
• *Trade & Security:* Xi urged closer economic dialogue and expanded cooperation on counternarcotics, immigration repatriation and combating telecommunications and online fraud.

*Wall Street issued fresh bullish calls across AI, software, semiconductors and infrastructure Thursday, although Daiwa sharply reduced its Nvidia target amid leadership and spending concerns.*

• *Connected Suppliers:* Maginfra, Singapore-based Kaytus and California-based Aivres distribute firmware 99.94% identical to IEIT's. Corporate records link Kaytus and Aivres to IEIT; none of the three is currently blacklisted.
• *AMD Partnership:* AMD lists Aivres as a supplier of servers using its Instinct AI accelerators. Aivres has also shipped billions in advanced computing equipment to Southeast Asia, including Nvidia-powered systems.
• *Unanswered Questions:* The investigation could not establish who supplied IEIT's firmware or whether licenses authorized its use. AMD had not answered those questions by publication.

AMD *($AMD)* faces additional regulatory risks as Washington expands restrictions on advanced AI chips reaching Chinese customers through overseas suppliers and data centers, potentially affecting billions in regional sales.

• *New Restrictions:* Effective November 19, advanced AI chips and servers shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil require additional U.S. licensing.
• *January Deadline:* A separate rule, suspended through January 10, 2027, could extend blacklisting restrictions to foreign companies at least 50% owned by sanctioned entities, potentially including IEIT-linked Kaytus.
• *Revenue Exposure:* AMD billed $7.75B, or 22.4% of 2025 revenue, to China and Hong Kong, plus $4.28B, or 12.4%, to Singapore. Billing locations do not establish final destinations or how much revenue is restricted.
• *Existing Impact:* AMD previously recorded approximately $800M in charges after U.S. licensing requirements affected its MI308 AI chips.
• ⁠*Sam Winter-Levy, Carnegie Endowment:* “The era when you could just sell to whoever you wanted and do whatever you wanted ... I think that's coming to an end.”

AMD *($AMD)* also maintains significant manufacturing and licensing relationships in China, creating additional exposure as U.S. technology restrictions tighten, according to Hunterbrook Media.

• *Manufacturing Dependence:* Two ventures controlled 85% by China's Tongfu Microelectronics handle most AMD chip assembly, testing and packaging. AMD owns the remaining 15% and had a $100M loan outstanding to one venture.
• *Blacklisted Ventures:* Hunterbrook linked $67M in AMD's 2025 licensing gains to Chinese chip ventures blacklisted in 2019. The payments may reflect pre-existing licenses and do not establish export violations.
• *Additional Connection:* AMD's February 2026 Instinct server catalog lists a Cancon system. Cancon is an alias of blacklisted Suma Technology, but the listing alone does not establish a transaction.
• *Investment Implications:* AMD's ambition to grow data-center AI revenue more than 80% annually over the next three to five years increases the importance of regulatory access and supply-chain continuity.
